prompt.context: During your weekly game of pickleball with the CEO of Puerto Pay, a Puerto Rican payments processor, she mentions that she is thinking of expanding her company's footprint and has been looking to acquire Telepay, a competitor based in Panama. She knows of your stellar reputation as a consultant and asks for you to determine whether or not she should acquire Telepay. Payment processors are technology companies that facilitate transactions between customers, merchants, and banks, and collect fees for facilitating these transactions. Both Puerto Pay and Telepay have the same product: Point-of-Sale (POS) systems. POS systems allow merchants to charge customers for transactions made in-store. Puerto Pay and Telepay have no overlapping customers. Telepay has over 85% of market share in Panama and can be considered to have a monopoly on the payments processing space in Panama (generating 100% of revenues of the Payment Processing market in Panama).
prompt.question: Should Puerto Pay acquire Telepay? Puerto Pay had profits of $625MM in 2020 and is looking to increase profit in 2021 post-acquisition to $645MM, including the cost of buying Telepay. The CEO does not want to spend more than $500MM on acquiring Telepay.

clarifying_info.q: What is the total size of the Central American payments processing market?
clarifying_info.a: The total size (in revenue) of the Central American market is $681MM.

clarifying_info.q: What share of the Panama market does Telepay own?
clarifying_info.a: Telepay owns 90% of the Panama market; the remaining 10% is fragmented among a handful of competitors.

clarifying_info.q: What is the acquisition cost for Telepay?
clarifying_info.a: Acquisition cost: EV minus Net Debt, times a control premium of 120% = $400MM x 120% = $480MM.

clarifying_info.q: How much does each of Telepay's server racks cost?
clarifying_info.a: Each server rack costs $1.25MM per year.

exhibits.title: Central American Payment Processing Market by Country (in Revenue, in $MM)
exhibits.shows: A pie chart showing the share of the Central American payments processing market by country, expressed as percentages.

exhibits.title: Telepay Costs by Department (in $MM)
exhibits.shows: A bar chart showing Telepay's annual costs broken down by department in $MM.

framework: External / Telepay Considerations: company profitability (revenue, costs, products), customer profile (demographics, loyalty, reputation), Panama market dynamics (growth rates, new competition domestic and international, macro trends)

Internal / Puerto Pay Considerations: deal financing (cash, debt, stock), synergies and cost-cutting (employee redundancies, IT/infrastructure consolidation, facilities consolidation), tax implications, branding, knowledge transfer, culture fit
Telepay Synergies: customer footprint, revenue streams, cross-sell opportunities, fee structures, bundling, NPV of synergies, upfront control premium
Puerto Pay Fit: physical capital, human capital, SG&A overlap, customer overlap
Risk: integration risk, company culture clash, talent departures, customer loss, regulatory/anti-competition issues, quality concerns

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 1, estimate Telepay's annual revenues.
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify Panama's share of the Central American market (33%), multiply by total market size ($681MM), then apply Telepay's market share (90%) to get revenues. Strong candidates will approximate cleanly.

math.setup: Panama share of CA market x Total CA market size x Telepay market share

questions.prompt: Given the acquisition cost, assess whether the price is acceptable relative to Puerto Pay's budget constraint.
questions.guidance: Candidate should calculate the acquisition cost using the formula provided and compare to the $500MM ceiling. $480MM is within budget but tight; candidate should flag this.

math.setup: EV - Net Debt = $400MM; apply 120% control premium
math.answer: Acquisition cost = $480MM, which is within the $500MM ceiling.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, identify the IT cost inefficiency and calculate potential savings.
questions.guidance: Candidate should notice IT spend ($85MM) is large. They should calculate how many server racks are actually needed for 24,000 TB of data at 500 TB per rack, compare to the 68 racks currently owned, and compute the cost of excess racks.

math.setup: Racks needed = total data / capacity per rack; excess = current racks - needed racks; savings = excess racks x cost per rack
math.answer: $25MM in annual IT cost savings by eliminating 20 unused server racks.

questions.prompt: Combining all figures, determine whether Puerto Pay can achieve its profit target of $645MM post-acquisition.
questions.guidance: Candidate should add Telepay's profit contribution (revenues minus costs) plus identified savings, then net out the acquisition cost. The casebook notes Telepay's 2020 profit was $52MM. Total combined profit should exceed $645MM.

math.setup: Puerto Pay 2020 profit + Telepay 2020 profit + IT savings - acquisition amortization or cost

brainstorming.prompt: What risks or concerns should Puerto Pay consider before proceeding with this acquisition?

categories.name: Regulatory / Legal
ideas: Antitrust scrutiny given Telepay's near-monopoly position in Panama
Anti-competition regulations could block or delay the deal
Additional compliance requirements operating across two countries

categories.name: Growth Limitations
ideas: Limited room to grow Telepay's revenue with 90%+ market share already captured
Dependence on overall Panama economic growth

categories.name: Integration Risk
ideas: Company culture clash between a Puerto Rican and Panamanian firm

categories.name: Financial Risk
ideas: $480MM acquisition cost is close to the $500MM ceiling — little margin for cost overruns
Financing structure (cash vs debt vs stock) affects balance sheet
Control premium may not be recoverable if synergies disappoint

recommendation: Recommend Puerto Pay proceed with the acquisition of Telepay
Telepay's 2020 profit of $52MM, combined with $25MM in IT cost savings and Puerto Pay's existing $625MM profit, yields a projected post-acquisition profit of ~$702MM — well above the $645MM target
The $480MM acquisition price is within the $500MM budget constraint
risks: Regulatory and anti-competition risk given Telepay's near-monopoly position
Limited organic growth upside for Telepay given its already dominant market share in Panama
next_steps: Conduct full due diligence on Telepay's financials and legal standing
Assess regulatory landscape in Panama for potential anti-trust issues
Develop integration plan focusing on IT infrastructure consolidation and culture alignment
Explore whether excess server capacity can be repurposed across the combined entity
